chapters.title: The Great Dinosaur Feast
chapters.text:
Rex was a big dinosaur. He had a mean face and a long tail.

One day, Rex was very hungry. He went to find food.

Rex saw a green plant. It was good to eat. He took a big bite. "Yum!" he said.

Then Rex saw a small animal. It ran away fast. Rex ran after it. His feet went boom, boom, boom!

Rex was so glad. Now he had a meal.

But wait! A loud sound came. It was another big dinosaur! She had sharp teeth and a loud roar.

Rex ran away as fast as he could. His friend was even bigger than him!

Rex found a safe spot. He sat and ate his meal in peace.

Dinosaurs were real animals long, long ago. They came in many sizes. Some were mean. Some were kind. But all of them were great!

chapters.title: The Dinosaur's Big Meal
chapters.text:
TRex was a big dinosaur. He would eat all day long.

One day, Trix the dinosaur said, "I am so hungry! I need a meal."

"Wait!" said Tex. "I can help you find food."

They went to look for plants. The plants tasted great!

"This meat is yummy," said Trix. "I will eat and eat."

"Look!" said Tex. "Leaves! Green leaves! They are so good to eat."

Both dinosaurs sat down. They had a big meal together. The food was so tasty. They could not wait for the next meal!

"This is the best day," said Trix. "Friends can eat and play."

Tex nodded. "Yes! We can wait for food. We can eat. We can be happy."

And so the two dinosaurs ate their meal and played in the sun. What a great day!

transcript.title: The Stegosaurus's Spiky Day
transcript.text:
A stegosaurus named Spike woke up one sunny day. He had big spikes on his back.

"Today I will play!" said Spike.

Spike went to eat some plants. The leaves tasted so good. He ate and ate all day long.

Then Spike heard a loud roar. "Oh no!" he said. "A mean T-Rex is near!"

Spike ran fast. His spikes stood up tall. The T-Rex could not catch him. Spike was too quick!

When it was safe, Spike went to find his friend. Her name was Trixie. She was a small green dinosaur.

"Let's go to the stream," said Trixie. "I need to get a drink."

They went to the cool stream. The water felt great. Spike and Trixie drank and splashed.

Then they sat in the sun. They could see the whole plain. It was so peaceful.

"Thank you for being my friend," said Spike.

"Thank you too," said Trixie.

When the sun went down, Spike felt so happy. It had been the best day of his life!

chapters.title: The Dinosaur's Dream
chapters.text:
Bea the dinosaur was very tired. She had to find a place to sleep.

Bea saw a big tree with lots of green leaves. The leaves were soft. She could make a bed under the leaves.

"I will eat a snack first," said Bea. She ate some plants. They were good to eat.

Bea lay down on her bed of leaves. It felt so soft and warm.

Bea began to dream. In her dream, she could fly! She soared high in the sky. She could see far away.

In her dream, she ate the best food. It was better than any real meal.

Bea woke up. The sun was here. Time to get up and play!

Bea was glad she had a nice dream. Tomorrow she would sleep again and dream once more.

transcript.title: The Triceratops and the Rain
transcript.text:
A triceratops named Thorn stood in a big plain. The sky was gray. He could feel the wind.

"Rain is coming," said Thorn. "I can tell."

Soon the rain began to fall. It came down fast. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter!

Thorn ran to find his family. He could see them by the rocks. "Come quick!" he called.

All the dinosaurs went to hide. They found a cave with a roof. It kept them dry and safe.

Inside the cave, Thorn's mom said, "Good job! You helped us all stay safe."

"How did you know the rain was near?" asked his baby sister.

"I felt the wind," said Thorn. "I saw the dark clouds. That is how we know."

The rain kept falling outside. The dinosaurs waited in the cave. They ate leaves and berries.

Then, after a long time, the sun came out. The rain had stopped.

"Let's go play!" said Thorn.

All the dinosaurs went back out. The plain looked so green and fresh. Puddles were all over the place.

Thorn jumped in a big puddle. Splash! The water went up.

"That was fun!" he said. His family laughed and played too.

chapters.title: The Dinosaur's Team
chapters.text:
One day, a big dinosaur saw green leaves on a tall tree. "I will eat those leaves!" he said.

He called his friends. "Come here! Let's team up!"

His friend Teal came fast. Teal was lean and mean.

"We can eat and eat," said the big dinosaur. "We can reach those leaves way up there!"

Teal said, "I had a dream. I dream we would eat the best leaves in the land!"

"Your dream came true!" laughed the big dinosaur.

They stood on each other. The big one was on the lead. He got one leaf. Then another leaf. Then ten more leaves!

"Yum!" they both said. "This team is great. We can eat so much when we team up!"

They ate and ate and ate. Their tummies were so full and so happy.

"Let's team up every day," said Teal.

"Yes!" said his big friend. "Team wins!"

transcript.title: Petra's Floating Boat
transcript.text:
Petra was a young dinosaur who loved to float on the water. She made a boat out of wood.

"I will sail far away," she said with a big smile.

She climbed into her boat. The water was calm and cool. She could see fish swimming near her boat.

Petra paddled down the stream. The current was slow and easy. Trees lined both sides of the water.

Then she saw something strange. A big shape was in the water!

"Oh no! What could that be?" said Petra. She felt a bit afraid.

But then she saw it was her friend, a kind Plesiosaur named Dale!

"Hi, Petra!" called Dale. "Want to sail with me?"

"Yes!" said Petra. She was so happy.

Dale swam next to her boat. Together they floated down the stream. They saw birds and plants and rocks.

When the sun began to set, they found a nice beach to rest.

"That was a great day," said Petra.

"Yes," said Dale. "We are good friends."

Petra felt so warm inside. Making new friends was the best thing of all.

transcript.title: Rex Learns to Roar
transcript.text:
Rex was a small T-Rex. He wanted to learn to roar like the big dinosaurs.

"Listen to my roar!" said Rex. But it was so quiet. It sounded like a small bird.

Rex felt sad. "I want a big roar," he said.

Then he met an old T-Rex named Roar. Roar was very big and strong.

"Can you teach me?" asked Rex.

"Yes, I can," said Roar. "First, you must feel brave. A roar comes from deep inside."

Rex took a deep breath. He thought about being strong and brave.

"Now open your mouth wide," said Roar. "Let the sound come out."

Rex opened his mouth. He pushed the air out hard. A loud sound came out!

"ROOOAARRR!" went Rex.

Roar smiled big. "That was a great roar! You did it!"

Rex felt so happy. He roared again and again. Each time, it got louder!

All the other dinosaurs came to hear Rex roar. They clapped and cheered.

"You are a real T-Rex now!" they said.

Rex stood tall and proud. He had learned something new. And he had made a good friend too.

transcript.title: The Long Neck's Great Feast
transcript.text:
Gina was a Brachiosaurus with a very long neck. She could reach the tallest trees.

"I am so lucky," said Gina. "I can eat leaves no other dinosaur can reach!"

One day, Gina woke up very hungry. Her tummy made a loud sound.

"Time to eat!" she said.

Gina walked to the tallest oak tree. She stretched her long neck up, up, up. The green leaves were right there!

Munch, munch, munch! She ate and ate. The leaves tasted so sweet and good.

Then Gina saw her friend Leo. Leo was a small Stego. He was looking sad.

"What is wrong?" asked Gina.

"I cannot reach the high leaves," said Leo. "All I can eat are the low plants."

Gina had an idea. "Wait right here!"

Gina reached way up high. She grabbed a huge bunch of fresh green leaves. Then she bent her long neck down low.

"Here you go!" said Gina.

Leo ate the leaves. "Oh, this is so good! Thank you, friend!"

Gina felt happy. Sharing with friends was even better than eating alone.

"Let's eat together every day," said Leo.

"Yes!" said Gina. "That is a great deal."

chapters.title: The Dinosaur's Dream
chapters.text:
One day, a small dinosaur had a big dream. He wanted to see the ocean and the beach. He said, "I will go find the sea!"

The dinosaur began to walk. Step, step, step. He saw green leaves on tall trees. The leaves moved in the breeze. He heard them rustle and squeak.

"Keep going!" said a bird. "The sea is far!"

The dinosaur did not get weary. He was neat and strong. He could make his dream real.

transcript.title: The Speedy Raptor's Race
transcript.text:
Speed was a small raptor. She was the fastest dinosaur in the whole plain.

"No one can beat me!" said Speed with pride.

One day, a new dinosaur came to the plain. His name was Flash. He was also very fast.

"Let's have a race!" said Flash. "We can race to the big rock by the stream."

Speed did not like this. She did not want to share first place.

"Okay," said Speed. "But I will beat you."

All the dinosaurs came to watch. They lined up by the start.

"Ready, set, go!" they called.

Speed and Flash ran fast. Their feet went boom, boom, boom! The ground shook.

Speed was in front. Flash was close behind. They ran and ran.

Then Speed felt her foot slip on some wet leaves. She almost fell!

Flash saw her slip. He could have passed her. But he did not. He slowed down to help her stay safe.

"Are you okay?" asked Flash.

"Yes!" said Speed. "Thank you!"

They ran side by side now. They were equal and fast.

When they got to the big rock, they stopped together.

"We both won!" said Flash.

Speed smiled. "You are a true friend," she said. "Being kind is better than being first."

chapters.title: The Dinosaur's Sail
chapters.text:
A big dinosaur had a long sail on his back. The sail was bright and wide. It could catch the wind and the rain.

"My sail helps me," said the dinosaur. "It keeps me cool in the heat. It shows other dinosaurs where I am."

One day, the sail got wet. Water went drip, drip, drip down his back. The dinosaur did not like it. He had to find shade.

He saw a tree with green leaves. The leaves made a good roof. He sat under the tree and waited.

Soon the rain began to slow. A cool breeze came through the leaves. The dinosaur felt better.

"My sail is dry now," he said with a smile. "It will help me play again!"

The dinosaur went back out to play. His sail went up and down, up and down, as he ran. It was a good day to be a dinosaur with a sail.

transcript.title: The Ankylosaurus and the Storm
transcript.text:
Stone was an Ankylosaurus. His body was covered in hard plates and spikes. He was very strong.

One day, the sky turned dark and gray. A big storm was coming.

"Everyone, take cover!" called Stone. "A storm is near!"

All the dinosaurs ran to find a safe place. Rain began to pour down hard.

Then Stone heard a small voice. "Help! Help!"

It was a tiny baby dino named Pip. Pip was stuck in some wet mud!

"Don't worry, Pip!" said Stone. "I will help you!"

Stone walked over to Pip. The rain was coming down so fast. But Stone did not slip or fall.

His hard plates kept him safe. His strong legs held him steady.

Stone reached down with his tail. Pip grabbed it tight.

"Hold on!" said Stone.

Stone pulled hard. Pip came out of the mud! They ran together to the cave.

Inside, all the dinosaurs were waiting.

"Thank you, Stone!" said Pip. "You saved me!"

"You are welcome," said Stone. "I am glad you are safe."

When the rain stopped, the sun came out. Pip played with the other baby dinos.

Stone felt proud. Being strong and brave meant helping others.

chapters.title: The Trail
chapters.text:
Mia and Kai went on a hike. They saw a big trail in the mud.

"Look!" said Mia. "What made this trail?"

Kai said, "It could be a dinosaur! Long ago, dinosaurs roamed the Earth. They left trails like this."

Mia felt the trail with her hand. It was deep and wide.

"Dinosaurs were so big!" said Mia.

They followed the trail. It went up a hill. It went around a tree.

"Maybe this dinosaur was looking for food," said Kai. "It ate plants and leaves."

Mia traced the trail with her finger in the air. She made the same path the dinosaur made long, long ago.

"I can see it!" she said. "I see the big dinosaur walking!"

Kai smiled. "You found a real dinosaur trail!"

They sat and drew pictures of the dinosaur that made the trail.

transcript.title: The Pteranodon's Sky Art
transcript.text:
Soar was a Pteranodon with big wings. She loved to fly high in the sky.

"I can sail through the air!" said Soar. "It feels so great!"

One day, Soar had a new idea. "I will paint the sky with clouds!"

She flew up, up, up into the blue sky. The air felt cool and clean.

Soar made big loops and turns. She made swirls and spins. Each move left a trail of white mist.

"Look! A giant bird!" called the dinosaurs below.

But it was not a bird. It was Soar making art!

She made a big circle. Then she made a shape like a heart. She made wavy lines that went back and forth.

"That is so pretty!" said her friend Dale, the long Plesiosaur.

Soar felt happy. She made one more shape. It looked like a big smile!

All the dinosaurs cheered. "More! Make more!"

Soar flew and flew. She made clouds that looked like trees and rocks and streams.

When the sun began to set, the sky turned orange and pink. Soar's art looked even more beautiful.

"Thank you for showing us this," said the dinosaurs.

Soar landed and smiled. "Art is for sharing," she said. "And sharing makes me happy."

chapters.title: The Goat and the Boat
chapters.text:
One day, a goat saw a boat by the road.

"I want to go!" said the goat.

The goat got in the boat. The boat began to float.

Splash! Water went over the side.

"Oops!" said the goat. "This is not good!"

But then the goat saw the ocean. Big rocks stood by the shore. The goat felt brave.

"I will float to the rocks!" yelled the goat.

The boat went slow. It went low in the water.

Then—thump! The boat hit a rock.

The goat hopped out. His feet hit the rock. Safe!

"What a trip!" said the goat. "I saw so much. The water was cold. The rocks were big. I was brave!"

The goat sat on the warm rock. He could see miles and miles of sea.

"This was the best day," he said. "I will go again soon."
